title: Deep Work Is Rare
coreMove: Notice when an organization rewards responsiveness instead of contribution, then stop mistaking the signal for the work.
sourcePressure: The source frame says modern organizations often reward shallow behaviors through constant connectivity and visible busyness.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version complains about interruption; the chapter must expose the incentive system that makes shallow behavior look valuable.

exampleSpecs.domain: a hospital quality-improvement team tracking response times
exampleSpecs.audience: a department lead whose dashboard rewards quick replies over resolved defects
exampleSpecs.stakes: infection-control fixes stall while everyone clears messages fast
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the lead circles a metric showing twelve-minute reply averages and asks where the actual defect closure measure went
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a quality dashboard projected above a table of unopened audit binders

exampleSpecs.domain: a public radio newsroom after a breaking-news drill
exampleSpecs.audience: an editor who rewards frantic channel activity
exampleSpecs.stakes: the station broadcasts a shallow update instead of verified local context
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she compares the chat transcript volume with the thin final script and sees the newsroom praised motion instead of reporting
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a printed rundown with three blank source fields highlighted in blue

exampleSpecs.domain: an architecture firm using billable status rituals
exampleSpecs.audience: a project architect whose design time keeps losing to visible coordination
exampleSpecs.stakes: a library facade decision remains unresolved before the client review
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he refuses to count a day of coordination pings as progress and reserves two uninterrupted hours for the facade section
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a facade elevation pinned beside a stack of coordination notes

exampleSpecs.domain: a university lab where availability is treated as mentorship
exampleSpecs.audience: a principal investigator whose open-door norm blocks manuscript thinking
exampleSpecs.stakes: a grant renewal depends on a clear methods argument
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she counts how many interruptions were praised as helpful and how many moved the renewal argument forward
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a grant draft open to the methods page with four sticky notes across the screen edge

exampleSpecs.domain: a logistics dispatch center ranking operators by radio availability
exampleSpecs.audience: a supervisor whose scoreboard favors constant airtime
exampleSpecs.stakes: route redesign work is ignored until fuel costs climb
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the supervisor adds a route-improvement result column beside the radio-response column and the top performer changes
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a dispatch wallboard flashing response times above a fuel surcharge notice

exampleSpecs.domain: a nonprofit fundraising office measuring donor-touch counts
exampleSpecs.audience: a development director whose staff is rewarded for contact volume
exampleSpecs.stakes: major-donor strategy never gets built because small touches dominate the week
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she asks a fundraiser to show which donor insight came from forty logged touches, and the silence reveals the metric problem
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a donor CRM screen sorted by number of touches instead of gift potential

skillTargets: separate responsiveness metrics from actual contribution
spot visible busyness masquerading as value
choose a metric or behavior that would protect depth

tryThisNowSpec: Look at one workplace metric or praised behavior and write what deep contribution it might be replacing.
